text:
Maya L: hi all  day 3 hiccup. trying to port-forward to a local DB emulator in `rl-data` but get a 403: 
```
error: port forwarding failed: pods "db-emulator-0" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:default:maya-sa" cannot create resource "pods/portforward" in API group "" in the namespace "rl-data"
```
Maya L: i can `kubectl get pods -n rl-data` fine after identity sync, but port-forward fails. anyone seen this?
Ben (DevEx): welcome Maya! port-forward requires the `create` verb on the pods/portforward subresource. run `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n rl-data --as=system:serviceaccount:default:maya-sa` to confirm.
Maya L: ran it: `no`
Ben (DevEx): that explains it. Some team namespaces lock down portforward for security. Two options: we can add a RoleBinding for your SA for that subresource, or you can use a personal sandbox namespace and use port-forward there.
Maya L: i'd prefer not to request infra changes if sandbox works. how do i create a personal namespace?
Sam K: i can provision `maya-sandbox` and bind `edit` to `system:serviceaccount:default:maya-sa` which allows port-forward. infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4799 to provision maya-sandbox (ETA ~5m).
Maya L: sweet. is there a less privileged role that still allows port-forward?
Ben (DevEx): yes, we normally create a Role with verbs: ["get","list","watch","create"] on resources: ["pods","pods/portforward"] in the namespace, then create a RoleBinding to your SA. it keeps other permissions minimal compared to `edit`.
Example Role YAML snippet (devops will apply):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: sandbox-portforward
  namespace: rl-data
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create"]
```
RoleBinding:
```
kind: RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: bind-maya-portforward
  namespace: rl-data
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: maya-sa
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: sandbox-portforward
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

Sam K: created maya-sandbox and bound `edit` to maya-sa. try `kubectl port-forward svc/db-emulator 5432:5432 -n maya-sandbox` once you deploy a local emulator there.
Maya L: i see the namespace, deployed the emulator, port-forwarding now works locally. thanks!
Ben (DevEx): quick checklist for future folks: (1) run `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n <ns>`, (2) prefer personal sandbox for debugging, (3) request a scoped Role for production namespaces only if security approves.
Maya L: noted. also filed a doc suggestion to the onboarding page to include the port-forward check. thanks team :raised_hands:
